pr_title: Add support for TLS and connectionless LDAP connections on Linux
pr_body:
May fix #43890.

This PR does a few things for LDAP support in Linux for System.DirectoryServices.Protocols:

- Replaces deprecated OpenLDAP methods `ldap_init` and `ldap_simple_bind_s` with `ldap_create` and `ldap_sasl_bind_s`, respectively. 
- Fixes a problem with setting the LDAP version on the connection by using `IntPtr` types rather than `int` directly.
- Adds support for TLS and connectionless LDAP connections.

The first two points are prerequisites for the ultimate goal, which is to add LDAP TLS support to Linux. Let me know if you want me to break this up into multiple PRs.

# Testing

I tested this using by running the `osixia/openldap` image with a TLS listener on 1636, and extracted the self-signed CA to a file:

```
docker run -p 1389:389 -p 1636:636 --name ldap -d --rm -e LDAP_TLS_VERIFY_CLIENT=never osixia/openldap --loglevel debug
docker exec ldap cat /container/service/slapd/assets/certs/ca.crt > /tmp/ca.crt
```

I set the LDAP client CA certificate path in `/etc/ldap/ldap.conf` so OpenLDAP would trust the self-signed certificate:

```
# /etc/ldap/ldap.conf
#...
TLS_CACERT /tmp/ca.crt
```

(I'm testing with OpenLDAP 2.10.12 on Ubuntu 20.04, in case paths for configs differ on different distributions.)
I also had to map the short container ID (e.g. `7fb28b4656af`) to `127.0.0.1` in `/etc/hosts`.

Finally, I ran `env LDAP_TEST_SERVER_INDEX=4 dotnet test` to select the new test configuration I added in `LdapConfiguration.xml` using TLS, and change the hostname to the short container ID in `/etc/hosts` to make sure the client validated the server certificate. All tests passed successfully locally, and I could see the successful binds and operations in the container logs.

issue_context.title: Add SSL support to LdapSessionOptions on Linux
issue_context.body:
<!--This is just a template - feel free to delete any and all of it and replace as appropriate.-->

### Description

When using System.DirectoryServices.Protocols.LdapConnection to connect to an LDAPS target on CentOS7, throws the error of

```
Unhandled exception. System.PlatformNotSupportedException: Operation is not supported on this platform.
   at System.DirectoryServices.Protocols.LdapSessionOptions.set_SecureSocketLayer(Boolean value)
   at activeDirectoryLdapExamples.Program.Main(String[] str) in /home/iguy/exceptionless/Program.cs:line 23
```

Example Code:
```
using System;
using System.Net;
using System.DirectoryServices.Protocols;

namespace LdapsExample
{
   class Program
   {
      static void Main(String[] str)
      {
            var ldapInfo = new LdapDirectoryIdentifier("1.2.3.4", 636);

            using (var ldapConnection = new LdapConnection(ldapInfo))
            {
              var nC = new System.Net.NetworkCredential("ldaps_login", "my_password");
               ldapConnection.AuthType = AuthType.Negotiate;
               ldapConnection.SessionOptions.ProtocolVersion = 3;
               ldapConnection.SessionOptions.SecureSocketLayer = true;
               ldapConnection.SessionOptions.VerifyServerCertificate += delegate { return true; };
               ldapConnection.Bind(nC);
            }
            Console.WriteLine("True");
      }
   }
}
```

Hello @iguyking, yes what you are seeing is expected as we currently don't support SSL on Linux yet. I believe that the native library that we use underneath in Linux does support SSL so it might just be a matter of exposing this functionality by calling the right native API on libldap. I found this interesting thread on the topic: https://www.openldap.org/lists/openldap-software/200603/msg00212.html more specifically :

```
>>OpenLDAP's -lldap supports initiating TLS (SSL) using either
>>the standard "Start TLS" mechanism [RFC2830] or the non-standard
>>"ldaps:" (Secure LDAP) mechanism.  In the former case, the
>>program should call ldap_initialize(3) with the appropriate
>>ldap: URL, set version to 3, and then call ldap_start_tls_s(3).
>>In the latter case, ldap_initialize(3) is called with the
>>ldaps: URL.  In both cases, appropriate certificate information
>>should be provided via ldap.conf(5) facilities or via
>>ldap_set_option(3)).  See the client/tools for example code.
```

I'll mark this issue as up-for-grabs in case anybody from the community wants to add this support to Linux before we get to it.

For anyone looking for a termporal fix until this gets implemented: [Novell.Directory.Ldap.NETStandard](https://github.com/dsbenghe/Novell.Directory.Ldap.NETStandard) supports LDAPS and LDAP+StartTLS.

Any idea if/when SSL will be supported in Linux?

Thanks

It is definitely doable which is why we've kept this issue open and it is in our backlog, but we don't have it planned for any release yet. That said, we are open for contributions which would be a good way of ensuring that this gets in sooner rather than later.
If I were interested in taking this on, where would I start?

In Linux, we use OpenLdap (libldap) native library as the underlying protocol implementation to communicate to ldap servers, so in order to add this support, I would imagine that there are mainly two aspects to check:
1- First, in terms of the actual setting of the option itself, you can start by checking the openldap manual here https://www.openldap.org/software//man.cgi?query=ldap_get_option&sektion=3&apropos=0&manpath=OpenLDAP+2.4-Release and take a look in particular to all of the options and settings that are related to SSL/TLS as we would have to be able to control some of those at least to enable SSL.
2- After that, we currently use [ldap_simple_bind](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/d2f75223e4845be6731282d12a3214a98d8faa18/src/libraries/System.DirectoryServices.Protocols/src/System/DirectoryServices/Protocols/ldap/LdapConnection.Linux.cs#L33) to perform the binding to the server with credentials, but we should probably need to switch to use the sasl bind instead if we wanted to use SSL although I'm not entirely sure of this. Here is more info on the different ways to bind to a server https://www.openldap.org/software/man.cgi?query=ldap_bind&sektion=3&apropos=0&manpath=OpenLDAP+2.4-Release 

That is where I would start with this, but not sure if that is all that would be needed. @flamencist might be able to tell if there are more things to be added apart from this.
Thanks! I'll take a look at this. I can't commit to implementing right now, so if someone else gets to it first, that's OK.

I may not see the whole picture are but for client side e.g. connection to secure server there should be no need for certificates (in most cases) 
I think the most difficult part is managing trust e.g. dealing with verifying server identity. As minimal, you can leave it OS and trust the server when OS does.  I think preferably, we would allow to specify [RemoteCertificateValidationCallback](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.net.security.remotecertificatevalidationcallback?view=net-5.0) delegate in way how SslStream does it.

@wfurt,

> I may not see the whole picture are but for client side e.g. connection to secure server there should be no need for certificates (in most cases)

I'm not sure I understand the comment. Do you mean there's no need to specify the CA if the server is signed with a trusted CA? I agree, and it seems to be the .NET way to defer all trust to the OS. (You know more about this than me! :smiley:  )

If you're reacting to the specification of the CA certificate in the sample code above, this was because I was testing with auto-generated, self-signed certificates. In this case, it was cleaner for my workflow to add the option inline than to continue adding certificates to the cert store.

> I think preferably, we would allow to specify RemoteCertificateValidationCallback delegate in way how SslStream does it.

That sounds like a great idea for flexibility. I saw some options to do that, but I didn't know how to wire it up across the interop layer. :slightly_frowning_face: 

@joperezr, is there something else I can do to move this along? We'd like to move some of our LDAP access code to Linux/containers and would prefer to standardize on System.DirectoryService.Protocols. But we also only follow the LTS releases of .NET, so I'm antsy to get this in before November.

I'm not familiar with the runtime internals, but I had a local branch with some hacks to make it work on the Linux platform. If someone is able to help mentor me, I think I could pull a PR together.
@joperezr, I've opened up #52904 to start off this process. You can also assign me to this issue for now.

review_comments: I must be missing something, but where is this used?

Not at all. It's probably supposed to be used to store this ptr: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/0fc56b96739bc378a73132932028fb0614d0c970/src/libraries/System.DirectoryServices.Protocols/src/System/DirectoryServices/Protocols/Interop/LdapPal.Linux.cs#L107

There seem to be two similar occurences of the code, one of which is looks correct:
- https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/0fc56b96739bc378a73132932028fb0614d0c970/src/libraries/System.DirectoryServices.Protocols/src/System/DirectoryServices/Protocols/ldap/LdapConnection.Linux.cs#L88-L103
- https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/0fc56b96739bc378a73132932028fb0614d0c970/src/libraries/System.DirectoryServices.Protocols/src/System/DirectoryServices/Protocols/Interop/LdapPal.Linux.cs#L104-L113

Maybe it could be interesting to deduplicate this?
I'm fine choosing to dedupe or not, I'll leave that to @iinuwa but at least we should fix the occurrence when we are not storing the pointer for the berval password.
Oh, sorry for the oversight. I went ahead and combined them since they're doing the same thing now.

> Fixes a problem with setting the LDAP version on the connection by using IntPtr types rather than int directly.

Could you say more?

In my testing, I had a problem where the version was not being set properly when using an integer rather than an IntPtr, so it was defaulting to LDAPv2 on my machine and failing to connect. The API calls for an pointer to an int:

> LDAP_OPT_PROTOCOL_VERSION
>              Sets/gets the protocol version.  outvalue and  invalue  must  be
>              int *.

I think this might work now because the value is being [cast to an integer pointer on the C side](https://git.openldap.org/openldap/openldap/-/blob/OPENLDAP_REL_ENG_2_4_58/libraries/libldap/options.c#L851-852), but from what I understand (which is very little) I think that this can fail on systems with different pointer sizes?
Does it matter that this will apply to all tests?

I don't think so? I think it just means that the `SecureSocketLayer` setter gets called twice with `false` (once in the constructor and again here) if `<UseTls />` is not set or is `false` in `LdapConfiguration.xml`. As long as that setter is idempotent, I don't think it causes any harm.

I can put a guard in though if that's safer.

Is it possible for `directoryIdentifier.Servers` to, through bad input, contains only servers that are empty strings? If so uris will be null but it appears openldap treats that as return to default. Not sure whether that's what you want, or you want to avoid calling it in that case.
https://git.openldap.org/openldap/openldap/-/blob/master/libraries/libldap/options.c#L655

Yes, it is possible. As you said, OpenLDAP falls back to its default hostname (which can be configured in `/etc/ldap/ldap.conf`) if the hostname is not set. I intentionally allowed that behavior here too since it would be expected if someone is familiar with OpenLDAP.

I _think_ that's OK... though I don't know how the Windows side handles empty string hostnames. If someone wrote code on Linux, then tried to run on Windows, that could be an issue if Windows doesn't support default hostnames.
do we have any test for connectionless?

No, I wasn't sure how to test it. I think that since connectionless LDAP isn't standardized, it's only implemented in AD (or as far as I can tell, it's not implemented in slapd). I've only got access to one [production] instance of AD, so I didn't want to test there! :)

I imagine that this is currently broken in Linux since there are no provisions anywhere else to configure connectionless. I think that this patch should work for connectionless _should_ work though.

Normally we don't add features we can't test 🙂. But if the feature is simply "given this flag, use this scheme prefix" maybe it's reasonable to add if testing isn't straightforward.

@joperezr preferences?
I agree that having a test would be ideally, but given the context here I think that if we can't come up with a good way to test this it may be reasonable.
